audit.why: 54.26% over 352 games. The chart hands Tryndamere levels 2-3 and both item stages, Camille the flat middle — which reads pessimistic against a 54% win rate, but the prose explains it: Camille's edge is the levels 4-5 tempo and closing the game, not the full-build duel. The shape is defensible and I am not moving it.

The level-6 spike is the best-argued entry in this matchup and it is mechanically right: The Hextech Ultimatum does not stop Undying Rage, so the sequencing is to chunk him below the immortality's value first and land the kill as it expires. Undying Rage is 120s at rank 1 down to 80s, which is worth stating — a Tryndamere who has spent it has ninety-plus seconds of being killable.

audit.whatIsWrong: Precision Protocol's recast is called a 'bonus-magic-damage second hit' in four places (spikes[1].text, wants.you[1], early, whys[1]). It is true damage, not magic. Tryndamere's passive is written as 'Build Fury' in wants.foe[0], his W is only 'W's slow', and Camille's passive is 'Adaptive Defense'.
audit.why: Riot flags Precision Protocol as true damage — that is the entire reason Camille beats a crit bruiser stacking armour, and calling it magic damage tells the reader MR matters when it does not. Riot's names are Battle Fury (P), Bloodlust (Q), Mocking Shout (W), Spinning Slash (E), Undying Rage (R). Mocking Shout is not just a slow: it reduces attack damage and only slows targets facing away, which is a real reason a fleeing Camille gets punished harder than an advancing one.
audit.corrected: True damage restored throughout; Battle Fury, Bloodlust, Mocking Shout and Spinning Slash named; Adaptive Defenses given its real name.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Don't burn your own E chasing into his W slow' and 'step back before his Fury and crit ramp' carry no numbers.
audit.why: Spinning Slash is 12s at rank 1 falling to 8s, against Hookshot's 16s — his gap-closer and escape are both back before yours, which is exactly why chasing him is the losing pattern this text is warning about. Bloodlust's active heal is 12s flat.
audit.corrected: Spinning Slash 12s vs Hookshot 16s written into early.

audit.whatIsWrong: Bloodlust's healing is called out three times as the thing that outlasts Camille's sustain, and Grievous Wounds is never mentioned.
audit.why: _missing-interactions.json flags Bloodlust sustain for this matchup specifically. Against a champion whose scaling plan is lifesteal plus an on-demand heal, anti-heal is the item decision the whole late-game section is dancing around.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds cue added to spikes[3].text.

edits.before: Level 1 is his — his auto plus a Fury-charged Spinning Slash out-trades your single Q before your Adaptive Defense shield is back off cooldown, so just farm and don't walk up. The lane flips at 2-3: once you have Q and a point in W you out-short-trade him hard. Land the re-cast Q for the bonus-magic-damage second hit and the move-speed boost, clip his outer hitbox with W to chunk his max HP and stick the slow, then step back before his Fury and crit chance ramp. Watch his E — he uses Spinning Slash to commit or escape, so don't burn your own E chasing into his W slow.
edits.after: Level 1 is his — his auto plus a Battle Fury-charged Spinning Slash out-trades your single Q before Adaptive Defenses can shield you again, so just farm and don't walk up. The lane flips at 2-3: once you have Q and a point in W you out-short-trade him hard. Land the delayed Precision Protocol re-cast for the true-damage second hit and the move-speed boost, clip his outer hitbox with W to chunk his max HP and stick the slow, then step back. Spinning Slash is 12s to your 16s Hookshot, so never spend your E chasing him into Mocking Shout.

notes: The load-bearing error was damage type: Precision Protocol's recast was described as bonus MAGIC damage in four places when Riot flags it as true damage. That inverts the itemisation logic — true damage is precisely why Camille beats a crit bruiser who stacks resistances, and the mirror audits for this champion (trundle, tahmkench) already state the true damage sits on Q and not on Tactical Sweep. 'Build Fury' was flagged by the packet as a suspect name and it is one: the passive is Battle Fury. Grievous Wounds against Bloodlust came from _missing-interactions.json and was absent despite three separate lines complaining that his self-heal outlasts her sustain.
